summary: First QA pass on Milestone 2 (accounts, tenancy, onboarding, versioned brief) against the public preview URL. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_m2_public.py (41 pytest cases over the real ingress with a cookie jar) covering signup/verification/outbox, login + lockout, onboarding persistence and row_version conflict, brief defaults, field-linked publish validation, publish v1/v2 immutability, reset-weights, locations (8 states, include/exclude conflict, radius, anchors), strict-schema rejections (extra workspace_id / value_score / bad mode), cross-tenant reads AND writes, anonymous 401s, sessions/profile/logout-all, password recovery, and the unsafe-route surface: 40 passed, 1 failed (login lockout). Re-ran tests/test_auth.py (10 passed) to prove the lockout logic works in-process, so the failure is environment-specific. Frontend: real-browser Playwright runs of signup -> verify-pending -> /dev/outbox -> verify (token single-use) -> sign in -> guided-setup redirect; 6-step wizard with 'Save and finish later', resume notice and 'Finish setup and open the brief'; brief editor (4 modes, Unknown help copy, field-linked blockers, publish disabled/enabled, publish twice + version history with actor email and reason, weights reset); locations (8 states, both-included-and-excluded error, radius, anchors Unknown notice); settings (profile persistence, session list with THIS DEVICE, revoke another session, sign out everywhere) ; forgot/reset password end to end (old password rejected, new accepted); anonymous deep link /app/brief -> sign in with ?next; and a responsive sweep of 8 new screens at 1440/1024/390/320. Two frontend issues and one backend issue found; every hard product rule held (Unknown never shown as pass/fail, no Value Score, no send/offer/billing/scrape route, synthetic banner everywhere, Google/Apple visible but disabled with the Gmail statement).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers through the public URL. _locked_out() keys on request.client.host + email, but the ingress presents rotating pod IPs (observed 10.208.134.74 and .75 alternating within a 7-request burst from one client), so the 5-failure counter is split across identifiers and 7 consecutive wrong passwords all returned 401 with no 429. LoginAttempt rows confirm two distinct identifiers for the same client. In-process tests pass, so the guard is effectively bypassed in the deployed environment. Suggested fix: key the lockout on the normalised email (optionally combined with the first hop of a trusted X-Forwarded-For) instead of request.client.host.

minor.issue: Sessions accumulate without a cap or pruning - 9 active sessions after repeated sign-ins from one device (each login always creates a new AuthSession). The Settings list becomes long and hard to reason about; consider pruning expired/duplicate user-agent sessions or capping the list.

Concurrency semantics are inconsistent: a stale expected_row_version correctly returns 409 (verified), but in a real two-tab browser test the second tab's 'Save draft' succeeded (last write wins), so one tab's edits can silently overwrite the other's. Worth confirming whether useBrief refetches row_version before saving by design.

ui_bugs.issue: Horizontal page overflow of 8px at 320 CSS px (documentElement.scrollWidth 328 vs clientWidth 320). Offenders: states-section, areas-section, anchors-section, locations-save and locations-publish-link all render 312px wide starting at x=16, i.e. the page container adds 8px more than the 16px gutters allow. Every other new screen (signup, verify-pending, dev outbox, forgot-password, onboarding, brief, settings) is clean at 320/390/1024/1440.

'Save and continue' is clickable before the journey has finished loading, so the request carries a stale expected_row_version and the API returns 409 'This journey changed in another session. Reload before saving again.' The wizard then stays on the step with the conflict banner and never refreshes row_version, so the only recovery is a manual reload. Disable the step buttons (or refetch on conflict) while the journey request is in flight - Supabase latency of ~1s makes this easy to hit.

At 320px the fixed bottom nav uses bg-surface/95 + backdrop-blur, so page content behind it bleeds through and the 'Today'/'Properties' labels look smudged/low-contrast in rendered screenshots. Consider an opaque surface for the mobile tab bar.

integration_issues.flow: Public pages (Welcome, signup, verify-pending, outbox, reset)
integration_issues.issue: Every public page load logs 2x console 'Failed to load resource: 401' from the unauthenticated GET /api/auth/me bootstrap, and the call is fired twice per load. Functionally harmless but it breaks the 'no console errors' bar from Milestone 1 and doubles a ~1s Supabase round trip on the sign-in screen; swallow the expected 401 and dedupe the bootstrap call.

issues: Numeric criterion inputs are exposed as land_sqm-min / land_sqm-max / floor_sqm-min (underscore) while the surrounding card is criterion-land-sqm and the QA notes documented land-sqm-min - inconsistent naming cost a test cycle. Normalise NumberField ids in BriefPage.numeric() to the hyphenated form (errors follow the same pattern, e.g. land_sqm-min-error).

action_items: Re-key login lockout so it is not defeated by rotating ingress client IPs (email-based identifier, optionally trusted X-Forwarded-For).
Fix the 8px horizontal overflow on /app/brief/locations at 320px.
Disable onboarding step buttons (or refetch row_version) while the journey request is in flight so 'Save and continue' cannot send a stale row_version and strand the user on a 409 banner.
Stop logging the expected unauthenticated /api/auth/me 401 to the console and dedupe the double bootstrap call on public pages.
Optional: normalise brief numeric-field test ids to hyphenated form; consider pruning/capping accumulated auth sessions.
critical_code_review_comments: app/api/auth.py:_locked_out/login - identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}" is not stable behind the k8s ingress; the lockout is therefore inert in the deployed environment even though tests/test_auth.py passes in-process.

app/api/auth.py:login - an unverified login records LoginAttempt(successful=True) before raising 403, which also clears nothing but does mean unverified-password guesses are not counted as failures; keep in mind when reworking the lockout key.

app/api/journeys.py:save_draft/publish rely on client-supplied expected_row_version only; the UI can send a stale value during initial load (observed 409) and, in another path, a second tab saved over the first. Decide on one policy (block or merge) and make the UI honour it.
features/brief/BriefPage.tsx:numeric() uses key.replace("_","-") for the card id but the raw key for field ids, producing mixed land-sqm / land_sqm-min identifiers.

success_rate.backend: 97.6% (40/41 pytest cases; the single failure is the login-lockout defect)
success_rate.frontend: 94% (all 15 requested flows exercised; 2 medium UI defects + 1 low + console-noise finding)

UI notes: (1) 'Publish version' opens a ConfirmDialog - click the trigger [data-testid="brief-publish"] then the dialog button named 'Publish version'; 'Sign out of all devices' confirm label is 'Sign out everywhere'; 'Request deletion' confirm label is 'Request deletion'. (2) Brief numeric inputs are land_sqm-min/-max, floor_sqm-min/-max (underscores), beds-min/-max etc.; locations editors are included-suburb/-postcode/-state/-add and excluded-* (not included-editor-*). (3) Because each API call costs ~1-1.5s, always wait_for_load_state('networkidle') plus ~2.5s before asserting on step titles, resume notices or blockers - short waits produce false negatives (a resume notice that looked MISSING at 2s was present at 4s). (4) The guided-setup redirect only happens when the account has zero journeys; once a journey exists, login lands on /app/today with a 'Resume setup' CTA (today-brief-cta).
rca_of_the_issue: Login lockout: app/api/auth.py builds the rate-limit identifier from request.client.host, which behind the preview ingress is the proxy pod IP. A single client's 7 consecutive failed logins were recorded under two identifiers (10.208.134.75 x2, 10.208.134.74 x5), so neither reached the 5-failure threshold and no 429 was returned; a DB probe of LoginAttempt confirmed the split. Reproduce with 6+ wrong-password POSTs to https://property-find-1.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login for one email. Mitigation: key on the normalised email (and/or the first hop of a trusted X-Forwarded-For) rather than the socket peer address. Onboarding 409: NewJourneyPage renders the wizard with a default/stale row_version before GET /api/journeys/{id} resolves; a click within that ~1s window posts the stale value, the server correctly rejects with 409, and the page keeps the stale value so every retry fails until reload.
